Aman,

Appreciate the clarity. High-level technical notes and recommendations below.

Quick pros/cons (short)
- VPC Peering:
  - Pros: simpler routing, lower latency, fewer managed endpoints to maintain. Good fit if FinPay can accept cross-account peering and route propagation.
  - Cons: requires configuration in your route tables and may need IAM/network approvals; no transitive routing.

- AWS PrivateLink (Interface VPC Endpoint):
  - Pros: tight control, no route table changes on your side, endpoint policies can be restrictive. Useful if security/compliance requires strict endpoint controls or if you cannot support cross-account peering.
  - Cons: higher operational overhead and slight added latency; additional cost for interface endpoints.

Egress / IP allowlist
- For initial pilot we can provide a short list of egress IPs. Tentative egress IP ranges (to be finalized by infra team):
  - 35.210.12.0/24
  - 35.210.13.0/24
  - 34.198.45.0/24

Note: these are placeholders for the pilot. For production we'll supply the finalized CIDR blocks (and can provide a signed attest if needed). If you choose PrivateLink, allowlisting is not required on your side for inbound traffic to our service; you still may need to manage outbound egress to external systems.

Config items we'll need from FinPay for peering:
- VPC ID(s) in us-east-1 and the CIDR blocks to avoid overlap
- Preferred peer account ID (if you want us to initiate)
- Route table IDs to add peering routes

I've attached a simple diagram (network-diagram.png) showing both options side-by-side. Happy to run through this on Thu 6/17 10:30am ET — invite received.


Sean
